_why:
The last fourteen edges carrying no note at all. Each is written from claims already verified and recorded on the two nodes it joins, and takes that node's own primary sources. No new research and no new assertion; this is the board saying out loud what it already holds.

Three are worth reading for themselves.

ACCM is the hole in the four-regime map. 32 CFR 117.23 puts Alternative Compensatory Control Measures in the same regulated set as SAPs, SCI, RD, FRD, TFNI and NNPI and names it first, but it is the only member of that set with no reporting statute attached - 10 U.S.C. 119, 50 U.S.C. 2426, 3348 and 3091a each key on 'special access program' or 'controlled access program', and a measure that is neither falls outside all four.

The AAWSAP contract does not appear in public federal contract data. An FPDS-NG ATOM query for PIID HHM402-08-C-0072 returns an empty feed.

And the Reid sequence is now a chain rather than three loose nodes: he co-sponsored the July 2008 appropriation language that funded the work, signed the 24 June 2009 letter asking for a restricted SAP, and DIA Info Memo U-09-2660 of 13 November 2009 refused it in terms - 'DIA cannot find adequate justification to establish' it - after which Lynn and the Director met him about it.

edges.note: AARO inherited the reporting line this assessment opened. The June 2021 preliminary assessment predates AARO and was built from UAP Task Force holdings; the ODNI 2022 annual report then carries a section headed 'Establishment of the All-Domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO)' recording that the Deputy Secretary directed USD(I&S) to stand it up. The institutional relation is succession, not authorship.

edges.note: Consecutive reports in the same statutory series. Sec. 6802's new 50 U.S.C. 3373(k)(1)(A) requires a joint DNI/SecDef report 180 days after enactment of the IAA FY2023 'and annually thereafter for four years', so these are the second and third of five, and the series has a written end rather than running indefinitely.

edges.note: The Manual implements the Directive. The 2010 directive sets SAP policy and defines the carve-out in its glossary; the four-volume Manual carries the operating detail - Volume 1's Enclosure 2 on DSS oversight and its relief, Enclosure 4 on whistleblower routing through SAP channels, and the patents and intellectual property provision. Directive states the policy, Manual runs it.

edges.note: The request and the refusal. Reid's 24 June 2009 letter asked for a restricted SAP; DIA Info Memo U-09-2660 of 13 November 2009 is the answer - 'DIA cannot find adequate justification to establish' it. DIA Info Memo U-10-2552 then records that Deputy Secretary Lynn and the Director met Senator Reid in November 2009 to discuss it. A documented request, a documented denial, and a documented meeting between them.
